$comment: Machine-readable, bounded allow-list for Cratis/Components#176. Every entry names the exact upstream package/version, the diagnostic codes it produces, why it is external to Components, and an objective, checkable removal condition. verify-public-types.mjs refuses to treat an unlisted diagnostic - or a diagnostic whose file does not match filePrefixes - as covered, and fails the run if a listed exception stops reproducing (the removal condition is presumed met and the entry is stale).

upstreamIssues.summary: pixi.js bundles @webgpu/types, whose WebGPU ambient declarations duplicate identifiers TypeScript 6 now ships in lib.dom.d.ts (GPUTextureFormat, GPUDevice, GPUBindGroupDescriptor.entries, ...) with incompatible shapes.
upstreamIssues.reason: external - upstream declaration collision between @webgpu/types (a pixi.js dependency) and TypeScript's own built-in DOM lib; not a Components authoring defect.
upstreamIssues.removalCondition: pixi.js ships a @webgpu/types release whose WebGPU surface no longer duplicates conflicting global identifiers against the target TypeScript version's lib.dom.d.ts (tracked upstream at https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs and https://github.com/gpuweb/types), OR Components narrows Canvas's public renderItem/CanvasContext contract off raw PIXI.* types without losing the ability to render arbitrary Pixi content (rejected for now - see docs/ui-foundation.md, 'Why the Canvas Pixi surface is not narrowed').

upstreamIssues.summary: @cratis/arc.react ships a global.d.ts that declares `namespace JSX` referencing test-only ambient types (vitest/globals, chai, sinon-chai) as part of its published package instead of scoping that augmentation to its own test build. A strict external consumer that does not also install those test packages cannot resolve the bare `JSX` identifiers arc.react's dialog/command declaration files reference.
upstreamIssues.reason: external - @cratis/arc.react's own shipped .d.ts, not a Components declaration; Components has no `namespace JSX` augmentation of its own.
upstreamIssues.removalCondition: A published @cratis/arc.react release removes (or properly scopes to its own test build) the global `namespace JSX` augmentation in global.d.ts, so `JSX.Element` in its public dialog/command declaration files resolves through @types/react's module-scoped JSX types instead.

upstreamIssues.summary: @cratis/arc, @cratis/arc.react, and @cratis/fundamentals publish ESM declaration files with extensionless relative specifiers (e.g. `export * from './ICommandScope'`). Node16/NodeNext module resolution requires an explicit extension on relative ECMAScript imports, so these upstream barrels fail under --moduleResolution nodenext; downstream symbols that transit through the broken barrel then read as missing (TS2305/TS2694 cascades).
upstreamIssues.reason: external - the extensionless specifiers live in @cratis/arc, @cratis/arc.react, and @cratis/fundamentals's own published dist, not in Components' declarations. Cratis/Components' own declaration rewrite (this PR) already eliminated Components' extensionless specifiers.
upstreamIssues.removalCondition: Coordinate with @cratis/fundamentals (and @cratis/arc / @cratis/arc.react, which share the same generator/build) to add explicit .js extensions to relative specifiers in published declaration files, per the issue's direction to fix this upstream rather than copy or patch their types in Components.
